name: ospren
author: rule-family designer (world: a 5x5 picture of marks; lineup answer, revision 3)
description: 5x5-PICTURE RULE-FAMILY class, REVISION 3 = A UNIVERSE OF RELATIONS (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. 'Revision 3 (2026-09-05)' and its 'Recipe for the other five lineup classes'; working notes and the full iteration record in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_pixels.md sec. 17-24; v1 kept as challenges/lab/ospren.v1.json, v2 as challenges/lab/ospren.v2.json). WHY v2 HAD TO CHANGE: in lad-ospren-v2-1 two Opus centaurs spent NO demo on ospren and scored 87 % and 80 % (target ~50 %). Their engine, in their own words: round 1 skip everything (~300 clues harvested free), round 2 answer a RANDOM candidate (k=4, so ~30 gold labels for nothing - "30x what a demo gives"), then per clue enumerate a bank of cheap grid predicates, keep those true of every example and of exactly one candidate, weight by rarity and answer the candidate the rarest survivor points at. It worked because EVERY RULE OF v2's U WAS ITSELF A PREDICATE IN THAT BANK: measured against an 811-predicate reconstruction of the two players' own 5x5 banks (ospren1a's f_ospren, 44 keys; ospren1b's f_ospren, 80 keys; plus the obvious extensions - per-row and per-column counts, the bounding box, which sides of the frame are touched, equal line pairs, 8-connected blobs, diagonal touching pairs), all 29 rules of v2's U have best Jaccard 1.00 (count of marks = 'k', symmetries = 'hmir'/'vmir'/'rot180', corners = 'corners', rows used = 'nrows', blobs = 'ncomp', biggest blob = 'maxcomp', lonely marks = 'niso', full lines = 'nfullrow'/'nfullcol', middle square = 'centre', equal rows = 'rowsame'). All 29 are RETIRED TO THE TRAP LIST. THE FIX (lever 3): U is now made of RELATIONS between two rows, two columns, a mark and its neighbour, or a line of marks and a wall - things a kid checks by eye in seconds and a per-picture feature bank cannot express, because they compare two parts of the picture instead of reading one number off the whole. UNIVERSE U: 12 templates, 33 rules, 27 of them relational (best Jaccard against the 811-predicate bank 0.17-0.40) and 6 CHEAP ones (Jaccard 1.00, kept on purpose at double draw weight as the learnable slope, 36.6 % of clues). Templates, with the parameter convention shared with the scorer (A = the rows if q<2 else the columns): (0) every row/column of marks reaches the left/right/top/bottom wall, q=0..3, density .108-.112; (1) every mark has a mark right beside it / right above or below it, q=0,2, .060-.062; (3) the first two rows/columns come back again as the last two, q=0,2, .021; (4) the top and middle / the middle and bottom row (column) are exactly the same, q=0..3, .116-.121; (5) two rows/columns next to each other are exactly the same, q=0,2, .277; (6) row q and column q have their marks in the same places, q=0..4, .112-.128; (7) in every row/column the marks are all in one piece, q=0,2, .307; (8) every row/column of marks starts in the same place, q=0,2, .153-.155; (9) every mark on the top/bottom/left/right wall has a mark just inside it, q=0..3, .198-.202; CHEAP (10) the picture is its own mirror / its own top-bottom flip, .057/.062; (11) exactly one row/column is completely full, .041; (12) exactly three / all four corners are marked, .057/.031. U IS AN ANTICHAIN: brute-forced over the 20 000-picture generator pool AND 150 000 uniform-random pictures - 0 nesting violations, minimum support 420 pictures in the pool. The examples and the true candidate of a template 3/4/6 clue are always drawn from pictures that satisfy it VISIBLY (the compared lines are not both empty), because "the top row and the middle row are the same" is technically true of two empty rows and a kid reading such an example learns nothing. CLUE LAYOUT, blocks separated by ONE BLANK LINE: 2 or 3 EXAMPLE pictures (five lines of five characters from '#' and '.'), then FIVE CANDIDATE blocks, each a line holding just its number 1..5 followed by the five lines of that candidate. ANSWER = the one candidate that obeys the hidden rule, written back verbatim (whitespace-insensitive, with or without its number line, or as one space-separated line) or as its 1-based index 1..5. THE LINEUP (revision 2 rules 1-5, 5b, 5c; revision 3 levers 1, 2, 5): exactly one candidate obeys R (500/500); all five candidates have the SAME NUMBER OF MARKS (500/500), which matches every count-shaped predicate of the bank and three of the trap families for free; all five fire EXACTLY the same example-consistent excluded rules - matched trap profiles in the STRONG form: over 500 clues all 3574 fitted traps are satisfied by all five candidates or by none (3574/3574), so no trap, no count of traps and no combination of traps separates the lineup and a player whose universe is U plus the traps is worth exactly a player who knows U; five distinct candidates, none of them an example (500/500 each); the minimal example set is a PAIR on 478 of 500 clues; the true candidate's position is uniform (109/96/94/107/94). AIMING (lever 5): generate carries the 811-predicate bank inside it (the 808 with base rate >= 1.5 % are given bit positions; the players floor their own frequency estimates at 5 %), intersects it over the examples, and aims the true candidate's rank at a uniformly random place in FOUR orders the attacker can build - the RARITY order (the surprise of the rarest bank predicate that picks it alone: this is what both revision-2 players actually ran), the COUNT order, the LOOK-ALIKE order (how much it shares with the other four) and the FAMILY-RESEMBLANCE order (how much it shares with its nearest example). THE ATTACK, SIMULATED (skip-harvest 300 clues for base rates -> answer a random candidate on a disjoint 1600 clues, keeping the ~1/5 that come back correct as gold labels and the wrong picks as negatives -> per-predicate unique-explanation weights -> rarity-weighted pick; 500 fresh test clues, seeds 1e6..1e6+499, live unfiltered feature bank): v3 scores 44.2 / 46.4 / 47.0 / 48.0 / 47.4 % at 0 / 30 / 60 / 120 / 240 labels - FLAT, which is the point - against v2 AS SHIPPED under the identical engine 76.8 / 87.3 / 85.3 / 87.8 / 88.0 % (the same engine scores 85 % where the real players scored 80-87 %, so it is a fair-to-slightly-strong model of an Opus centaur). LEVER ABLATION (identical conditions, 400 test clues, 60 labels): v3 as shipped 47.2 %; minus lever 3 (v2's own universe) 85.3 %; minus lever 5 (decoys not aimed) 54.2 %; minus lever 1 (k=4) 51.0 %; lever 1 pushed (k=6) 44.5 %; minus lever 2 (three-example clues) 44.8 %. So the relational universe is worth ~38 points, the aiming ~7, the fifth candidate ~4; k=6 buys 2.7 points but costs a clue block and a kid's patience, and three-example clues buy 2.4 points but lengthen the clue - both were declined. THE CEILING STAYS WHERE IT BELONGS: the IN-U INTERSECTION IS 100.0 % - a player who has mapped U wins every clue - and an attacker whose bank also contains all of U scores 82.8 / 87.2 / 88.6 / 90.0 / 91.4 % at 0/30/60/120/240 labels and learns U to 90 % coverage in ~360 labels. With the generic bank alone, coverage can never pass the three cheap templates (36.6 % of clues). The gap 47 % -> 90 % IS the class, and it is paid for by inventing the vocabulary: looking at two little pictures and thinking "the top row and the middle row", "every column stands on the floor". DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (never in U; learning what this class never says is the game): 31 trap families, 29 of them v1/v2's own rules or v2's own trap list - exactly n marks / at least n / at most n / every square marked in all the examples / the picture is its own mirror, flip or half turn / exactly n corners / the marks sit in exactly n rows or columns / exactly n blobs / the biggest blob is n / exactly n marks stand alone / exactly one row or column is full / the middle square is marked or empty / every row has the same number / every column does / there is a mark in the middle column / every row has a mark / as many marks above the middle row as below / as many left as right / the four corners are all the same / the top row is the same as the bottom row / the first column is the same as the last / the top row is empty / no two marks touch / the picture touches the frame on exactly n sides / the picture has a hole / the longest straight run is n. Mean 7.15 of them fit any one clue (min 3, max 14); a trap that IS the hidden rule (only possible for the three cheap templates) is dropped from the profile, because a player who forms it has found the rule. WITNESSES over 500 fresh clues (floor 1/5 = 20 %): the true rule (solve) 100.0 %; the in-U intersection 100.0 %; a player who knows U minus two templates 80.6-93.2 % (median 86.8); the full revision-3 attack 44.2-48.0 %; the rarest unique surviving bank predicate 44.8 %; the candidate with the most touching pairs 30.8 %; the fewest lonely marks 30.6 %; the longest straight run 30.4 %; the most marked corners 30.4 %; the odd one out 28.6 %; the fewest lumps 27.6 %; the candidate least like an example 25.0 %; MOST surviving bank predicates 24.2 % (a decoy strictly out-counts the truth on 74.0 % of clues, where revision 2 rule 2 asks for >= 40 %); pick candidate 1 21.8 %; the candidate most like an example 20.2 %; a random candidate 19.0 %; each of the 21 trap families that ever fit 0-33 % (pure random tie-breaking: with all-or-none profiles the trap picks uniformly among the five, and the spread is sampling noise on 1-330 fits); the medoid 15.2 %. THE INSTANCE DISTRIBUTION: every example and every candidate is drawn from one mixture of little pictures (scattered marks, grown lumps, a few repeated row or column patterns, a mirrored half, stacks standing against a wall; 3-14 marks), never from uniform noise - measured, uniform noise makes the relations astronomically rare (gravity .006, repeated halves .004) and gives a kid nothing to look at. MEASURED over 500 clues: uniqueness 500/500, minimality 500/500, exactly one candidate obeys R 500/500, all five the same number of marks 500/500, five distinct candidates 500/500, no candidate equal to an example 500/500, matched trap profiles 500/500 (3574/3574 individual traps all-or-none), examples per clue 2 -> 478, 3 -> 22, all 33 rules drawn, 20 000 distinct clues and 0 fallback clues over 20 000 seeds. Clue 225-256 chars, answer 29 chars (or 1). generate 2.45 ms mean / 1.76 ms median / 11.3 ms p99 / 24.9 ms max over 5000 seeds (cap 100); the 20 000-picture pool with its 33-bit U mask, trap readouts and 808-bit bank mask costs about 6 s once per worker at module level and is not charged to max_generate_ms. solve 0.088 ms mean, score 0.083 ms mean. generate is deterministic across processes and hash seeds (md5 of the first 200 clues identical under PYTHONHASHSEED 0 / 1 / 12345). SCORE is 1017 chars (v2: 899; needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it splits the clue on blank lines, takes the last five blocks as the lineup, resolves the answer to one of them, rebuilds all 33 rules of U from a 33-character table (one character per rule, chr(48 + 5*template + parameter)) and one 13-branch predicate function, filters them by the examples, insists on a single survivor and asks whether the chosen candidate obeys it. Checked candidate-by-candidate against solve on 600 clues x 5 candidates x 7 answer forms (verbatim, index, index with spaces, candidate with its number line, one space-separated line, trailing newline, surrounding spaces) - 21 000 checks, 0 disagreements - and returns 0 without raising for '', 'x', '0', '6', '9', '55', '1 2', '1'x100, '#'x4000, '-1', '1.0', the unicode digits, a well-formed all-marks picture that is not in the lineup, the clue itself, the example block alone and one example. No hidden channel. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns the true candidate verbatim - it constructs nothing, so there is nothing to leak. RISK, named: the class is on the EASY side of the band (47 % simulated at 60 labels, target 35-55 %). If it comes back too easy the lever is to drop the three cheap templates to single draw weight (measured: 30.8 % of clues, attack 43.5 / 45.0 / 45.3 % at 0/30/60 labels); if too hard, k = 4 (+3.8 points) or three-example clues.

# --- the world: a 5x5 picture, five lines of five characters, '#' = a mark ---------------
# A picture is a 25-bit int, bit r*5+c.  Everything below works on the five row strings.
def ROWS(g):
    return ["".join("#" if g >> (r * 5 + c) & 1 else "." for c in range(5)) for r in range(5)]


# --- the universe U, REVISION 3: 12 templates, 33 rules -----------------------------------
# 27 of the 33 are RELATIONS between two rows, two columns, a mark and its neighbour, or a
# line of marks and a wall, rather than one number read off the whole picture, so they are
# absent from the generic 5x5 predicate banks the revision-2 players brought (best Jaccard
# against the 811-predicate bank below: 0.17-0.40, against 1.00 for EVERY rule of v2's U,
# which is why v2's whole universe is retired to the trap list).  Three CHEAP templates
# (mirror/flip, exactly one full line, three or four corners) are kept on purpose as the
# learnable slope and as continuity with v1/v2; they are drawn at double weight.
# Parameter convention, shared with score(): A = the rows if q < 2 else the columns.
#  0 every row/column of marks reaches the left/right/top/bottom wall   q = 0,1,2,3
#  1 every mark has a mark right beside it (q=0) / right above or below it (q=2)
#  3 the first two rows/columns come back again as the last two         q = 0,2
#  4 the top and middle / middle and bottom row (column) are the same   q = 0,1,2,3
#  5 two rows/columns next to each other are exactly the same           q = 0,2
#  6 row q and column q have their marks in the same places             q = 0..4
#  7 in every row/column the marks are all in one piece                 q = 0,2
#  8 every row/column of marks starts in the same place                 q = 0,2
#  9 every mark on the top/bottom/left/right wall has one just inside   q = 0,1,2,3
# 10 CHEAP: the picture is its own mirror (q=0) / its own top-bottom flip (q=1)
# 11 CHEAP: exactly one row (q=0) / column (q=2) is completely full
# 12 CHEAP: exactly q corners are marked                                q = 3,4
U = ([(0, q) for q in range(4)] + [(1, q) for q in (0, 2)] + [(3, q) for q in (0, 2)]
     + [(4, q) for q in range(4)] + [(5, q) for q in (0, 2)] + [(6, q) for q in range(5)]
     + [(7, q) for q in (0, 2)] + [(8, q) for q in (0, 2)] + [(9, q) for q in range(4)]
     + [(10, q) for q in (0, 1)] + [(11, q) for q in (0, 2)] + [(12, q) for q in (3, 4)])
CHEAP = (10, 11, 12)


def P(t, q, w, C):
    """Is the picture w (five row strings, C = its five column strings) an instance of the
    rule (t, q)?  The same table the scorer rebuilds from a 33-character string."""
    A = (w, C)[q > 1]
    if t == 0:
        return all("#" not in x or x[q % 2 * 4] == "#" for x in A)
    if t == 1:
        return all(len(y) - 1 for x in A for y in x.split("."))
    if t == 3:
        return A[:2] == A[3:]
    if t == 4:
        i = q % 2 * 2
        return A[i] == A[i + 2]
    if t == 5:
        return any(x == y != "....." for x, y in zip(A, A[1:]))
    if t == 6:
        return w[q] == C[q]
    if t == 7:
        return all("." not in x.strip(".") for x in A)
    if t == 8:
        S = [x for x in A if "#" in x]
        return len(S) > 1 == len({x.find("#") for x in S})
    if t == 9:
        i = q % 2 * 4
        X = A[i]
        return "#" in X and ("#", ".") not in zip(X, A[1 + i // 2])
    if t == 10:
        X = (C, w)[q]
        return X[::-1] == X
    if t == 11:
        return A.count("#####") == 1
    return (w[0][::4] + w[4][::4]).count("#") == q


def MASKOF(g):
    w = ROWS(g)
    C = ["".join(x) for x in zip(*w)]
    m = 0
    for j, r in enumerate(U):
        if P(r[0], r[1], w, C):
            m |= 1 << j
    return m


# --- blobs, used only by the trap features (never by a rule of U) -------------------------
def BLOBS(S):
    S = set(S)
    out = []
    while S:
        p = S.pop()
        st = [p]
        cur = [p]
        while st:
            r, c = st.pop()
            for q in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                if q in S:
                    S.discard(q)
                    st.append(q)
                    cur.append(q)
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def XFEAT(g):
    """What the EXCLUDED (trap) rules read off a picture -- v2's entire universe plus v2's
    own exclusion list.  Index 27 is the picture itself."""
    w = ROWS(g)
    C = ["".join(x) for x in zip(*w)]
    rc = [x.count("#") for x in w]
    cc = [x.count("#") for x in C]
    S = [(r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5) if w[r][c] == "#"]
    B = BLOBS(S)
    sz = [len(x) for x in B]
    run = 0
    for x in w + C:
        for y in x.split("."):
            run = max(run, len(y))
    SS = set(S)
    adj = sum(1 for r, c in S if (r + 1, c) in SS) + sum(1 for r, c in S if (r, c + 1) in SS)
    W = set((r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5)) - SS
    holes = 0
    for x in BLOBS(W):
        if not any(r in (0, 4) or c in (0, 4) for r, c in x):
            holes += 1
    co = w[0][::4] + w[4][::4]
    return (len(S), int(all(x == x[::-1] for x in w)), int(w == w[::-1]),
            int([x[::-1] for x in w[::-1]] == w), co.count("#"),
            sum(1 for x in rc if x), sum(1 for x in cc if x),
            len(B), max(sz) if sz else 0, sum(1 for x in sz if x == 1),
            rc.count(5), cc.count(5), int(w[2][2] == "#"),
            int(len(set(rc)) == 1), int(len(set(cc)) == 1),
            int("#" in C[2]), int(min(rc) > 0),
            int(rc[0] + rc[1] == rc[3] + rc[4]), int(cc[0] + cc[1] == cc[3] + cc[4]),
            int(co[0] == co[1] == co[2] == co[3]),
            int(w[0] == w[4]), int(C[0] == C[4]), int(rc[0] == 0), int(adj == 0),
            (rc[0] > 0) + (rc[4] > 0) + (cc[0] > 0) + (cc[4] > 0), int(holes > 0), run, g)


def TRAPS(X, rule):
    """The EXCLUDED rules -- never in U -- that are consistent with EVERY example (X = the
    examples' XFEATs).  Twenty-nine of the thirty-one families are v1/v2's own rules or v2's
    own trap list; a trap that IS the hidden rule (only possible for the three cheap
    templates) is dropped, because a player who forms it has found the rule."""
    t = [(0, min(x[0] for x in X)), (1, max(x[0] for x in X))]   # at least / at most n marks
    if len(set(x[0] for x in X)) == 1:
        t.append((2, X[0][0]))                                   # exactly n marks
    A = X[0][27]
    for x in X[1:]:
        A &= x[27]
    t.append((3, A))                        # every square marked in all of them is marked
    for i, cd in ((1, 4), (2, 5), (3, 6)):  # its own mirror / flip / half turn
        if all(x[i] for x in X) and not (rule[0] == 10 and cd == 4 + rule[1]):
            t.append((cd, i))
    for i, cd in ((4, 7), (5, 8), (6, 9), (7, 10), (8, 11), (9, 12), (24, 13), (26, 14)):
        # exactly n corners / rows used / columns used / blobs / biggest blob / lonely marks
        # / sides of the frame touched / longest straight run
        if len(set(x[i] for x in X)) == 1 and not (cd == 7 and rule == (12, X[0][4])):
            t.append((cd, i, X[0][i]))
    for i, cd in ((10, 15), (11, 16)):      # exactly one full row / column
        if all(x[i] == 1 for x in X) and not (rule[0] == 11 and cd == 15 + rule[1] // 2):
            t.append((cd, i))
    for i, cd in ((12, 17), (13, 18), (14, 19), (15, 20), (16, 21), (17, 22), (18, 23),
                  (19, 24), (20, 25), (21, 26), (23, 27), (25, 28)):
        # the middle square is marked / every row the same number / every column the same
        # number / a mark in the middle column / every row has one / as many marks above the
        # middle row as below / as many left as right / the four corners alike / the top row
        # is the same as the bottom row / the first column is the same as the last / no two
        # marks touch / the picture has a hole
        if all(x[i] for x in X):
            t.append((cd, i))
    if not any(x[12] for x in X):
        t.append((29, 12))                  # the middle square is empty
    if all(x[22] for x in X):
        t.append((30, 22))                  # the top row is empty
    return t


def TBITS(t, x):
    m = 0
    for k, c in enumerate(t):
        h = c[0]
        if h == 0:
            b = x[0] >= c[1]
        elif h == 1:
            b = x[0] <= c[1]
        elif h == 2:
            b = x[0] == c[1]
        elif h == 3:
            b = (x[27] & c[1]) == c[1]
        elif h == 29:
            b = not x[12]
        elif h == 30:
            b = bool(x[22])
        elif len(c) == 3:
            b = x[c[1]] == c[2]
        else:
            b = bool(x[c[1]])
        if b:
            m |= 1 << k
    return m


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE ATTACKER'S BANK, rebuilt inside the challenge: the union of the two 5x5 feature banks
# the revision-2 players actually brought (ospren1a's f_ospren, 44 keys; ospren1b's
# f_ospren, 80 keys) plus the obvious extensions a second round adds (the count in each
# individual row and column, the bounding box, which sides of the frame are touched, equal
# line pairs, 8-connected blobs, the smallest blob, diagonal touching pairs).  153 feature
# keys, ~810 realised (key, value) predicates over the pool.  The lineup is aimed against
# it -- see RANKS.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def FEAT(g):
    f = {}
    w = ROWS(g)
    C = ["".join(x) for x in zip(*w)]
    S = [(r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5) if w[r][c] == "#"]
    SS = set(S)
    k = len(S)
    rc = [x.count("#") for x in w]
    cc = [x.count("#") for x in C]
    f["k"] = k
    for m in (2, 3, 4, 5):
        f["k%%%d" % m] = k % m
    for t in range(2, 17):
        f["kge%d" % t] = k >= t
        f["kle%d" % t] = k <= t
    f["hmir"] = all(x == x[::-1] for x in w)
    f["vmir"] = w == w[::-1]
    f["rot180"] = [x[::-1] for x in w[::-1]] == w
    f["tr"] = C == w
    f["atr"] = [x[::-1] for x in C[::-1]] == w
    f["rot90"] = C[::-1] == w
    f["anysym"] = f["hmir"] or f["vmir"]
    f["allsym"] = f["hmir"] and f["vmir"]
    f["nsym"] = f["hmir"] + f["vmir"] + f["rot180"] + f["tr"] + f["atr"]
    f["nrows"] = sum(1 for x in rc if x)
    f["ncols"] = sum(1 for x in cc if x)
    f["nemptyrow"] = 5 - f["nrows"]
    f["nemptycol"] = 5 - f["ncols"]
    f["nfullrow"] = rc.count(5)
    f["nfullcol"] = cc.count(5)
    f["hasfullrow"] = f["nfullrow"] > 0
    f["hasfullcol"] = f["nfullcol"] > 0
    f["rmin"] = min(rc); f["rmax"] = max(rc); f["cmin"] = min(cc); f["cmax"] = max(cc)
    f["rowsame"] = len(set(rc)) == 1
    f["colsame"] = len(set(cc)) == 1
    f["nrowsame"] = len(set(rc)); f["ncolsame"] = len(set(cc))
    f["rowc"] = tuple(rc); f["colc"] = tuple(cc)
    f["rowc_sorted"] = tuple(sorted(rc)); f["colc_sorted"] = tuple(sorted(cc))
    f["rowparity"] = tuple(x % 2 for x in rc); f["colparity"] = tuple(x % 2 for x in cc)
    f["nrowsodd"] = sum(1 for x in rc if x % 2); f["ncolsodd"] = sum(1 for x in cc if x % 2)
    f["allrowsodd"] = all(x % 2 for x in rc); f["allrowseven"] = all(x % 2 == 0 for x in rc)
    f["rowsorted"] = all(rc[i] <= rc[i + 1] for i in range(4))
    f["evenrows"] = rc[0] + rc[2] + rc[4]
    f["ndistrow"] = len(set(w)); f["ndistcol"] = len(set(C))
    f["rowsdistinct"] = len(set(w)) == 5
    f["npalrow"] = sum(1 for x in w if x == x[::-1])
    f["npalcol"] = sum(1 for x in C if x == x[::-1])
    for i in range(5):
        f["row%d" % i] = rc[i]
        f["col%d" % i] = cc[i]
    f["centre"] = int(w[2][2] == "#")
    co = w[0][::4] + w[4][::4]
    f["corners"] = co.count("#")
    f["cornerpat"] = co
    f["border"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r in (0, 4) or c in (0, 4))
    f["inner"] = k - f["border"]
    f["nedge"] = f["border"]
    f["top"] = rc[0] + rc[1]; f["bot"] = rc[3] + rc[4]
    f["left"] = cc[0] + cc[1]; f["right"] = cc[3] + cc[4]
    f["topbot"] = f["top"] == f["bot"]; f["leftright"] = f["left"] == f["right"]
    f["diag"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r == c)
    f["antid"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r + c == 4)
    f["q00"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r < 2 and c < 2)
    f["q01"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r < 2 and c > 2)
    f["q10"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r > 2 and c < 2)
    f["q11"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if r > 2 and c > 2)
    f["qsorted"] = tuple(sorted((f["q00"], f["q01"], f["q10"], f["q11"])))
    par = sum(1 for r, c in S if (r + c) % 2 == 0)
    f["parA"] = par; f["parB"] = k - par; f["onepar"] = par == 0 or par == k
    f["halffull"] = k * 2 > 25
    B = BLOBS(S)
    sz = sorted(len(x) for x in B)
    f["ncomp"] = len(B)
    f["maxcomp"] = sz[-1] if sz else 0
    f["mincomp"] = sz[0] if sz else 0
    f["compsizes"] = tuple(sz)
    f["connected"] = len(B) == 1
    f["niso"] = sz.count(1)
    f["noadj"] = f["niso"] == k
    seen = set()
    n8 = 0
    m8 = 0
    for p in S:
        if p in seen:
            continue
        n8 += 1
        st = [p]
        seen.add(p)
        sz8 = 0
        while st:
            r, c = st.pop()
            sz8 += 1
            for a in (-1, 0, 1):
                for b in (-1, 0, 1):
                    q = (r + a, c + b)
                    if q in SS and q not in seen:
                        seen.add(q)
                        st.append(q)
        m8 = max(m8, sz8)
    f["ncomp8"] = n8
    f["maxcomp8"] = m8
    f["adjpairs"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if (r + 1, c) in SS) + sum(1 for r, c in S if (r, c + 1) in SS)
    f["diagpairs"] = sum(1 for r, c in S if (r + 1, c + 1) in SS) + sum(1 for r, c in S if (r + 1, c - 1) in SS)
    f["nadj0"] = f["adjpairs"] == 0
    f["n2x2"] = sum(1 for r in range(4) for c in range(4)
                    if (r, c) in SS and (r + 1, c) in SS and (r, c + 1) in SS and (r + 1, c + 1) in SS)
    f["has2x2"] = f["n2x2"] > 0
    mr = mc = 0
    for x in w:
        for y in x.split("."):
            mr = max(mr, len(y))
    for x in C:
        for y in x.split("."):
            mc = max(mc, len(y))
    f["maxrunrow"] = mr; f["maxruncol"] = mc; f["maxrun"] = max(mr, mc)
    f["deg"] = tuple(sorted(sum(1 for q in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)) if q in SS)
                            for r, c in S))
    W = set((r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5)) - SS
    wb = BLOBS(W)
    f["ncomp0"] = len(wb)
    f["nholes"] = sum(1 for x in wb if not any(r in (0, 4) or c in (0, 4) for r, c in x))
    if S:
        r0 = min(r for r, c in S); r1 = max(r for r, c in S)
        c0 = min(c for r, c in S); c1 = max(c for r, c in S)
        f["bw"] = c1 - c0 + 1; f["bh"] = r1 - r0 + 1
        f["barea"] = f["bw"] * f["bh"]; f["btop"] = r0; f["bleft"] = c0
        f["bfull"] = f["barea"] == k
    f["ttop"] = rc[0] > 0; f["tbot"] = rc[4] > 0
    f["tleft"] = cc[0] > 0; f["tright"] = cc[4] > 0
    f["nsides"] = f["ttop"] + f["tbot"] + f["tleft"] + f["tright"]
    f["toprow"] = w[0]; f["botrow"] = w[4]; f["leftcol"] = C[0]; f["rightcol"] = C[4]
    f["tb_same"] = w[0] == w[4]
    f["lr_same"] = C[0] == C[4]
    f["neqrowpairs"] = sum(1 for i in range(5) for j in range(i + 1, 5) if w[i] == w[j])
    f["neqcolpairs"] = sum(1 for i in range(5) for j in range(i + 1, 5) if C[i] == C[j])
    f["emptyrows"] = tuple(i for i in range(5) if rc[i] == 0)
    f["emptycols"] = tuple(i for i in range(5) if cc[i] == 0)
    f["nsinglerow"] = rc.count(1); f["nsinglecol"] = cc.count(1)
    return f


# --- the instance distribution: little pictures, not TV static ----------------------------
# Every example and every candidate is drawn from exactly this mixture, so nothing about a
# picture's provenance separates the truth from a decoy.  Scattered marks alone would make
# every relation astronomically rare (measured: gravity .006, repeated halves .004) and
# would give a kid nothing to look at.
def DRAW(r):
    m = r.randrange(100)
    g = 0
    if m < 40:
        for i in r.sample(range(25), r.randrange(3, 13)):
            g |= 1 << i
    elif m < 58:
        for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 4)):
            p = r.randrange(25)
            g |= 1 << p
            rr, cc = divmod(p, 5)
            for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 6)):
                d = r.choice(((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)))
                rr = min(4, max(0, rr + d[0])); cc = min(4, max(0, cc + d[1]))
                g |= 1 << (rr * 5 + cc)
    elif m < 72:
        pats = [r.randrange(1, 32) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 4))] + [0]
        for rr in range(5):
            g |= r.choice(pats) << (rr * 5)
    elif m < 82:
        pats = [r.randrange(1, 32) for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 4))] + [0]
        for cc in range(5):
            p = r.choice(pats)
            for rr in range(5):
                if p >> rr & 1:
                    g |= 1 << (rr * 5 + cc)
    elif m < 90:
        h = 0
        for i in range(25):
            if r.random() < .3:
                h |= 1 << i
        g = h
        for i in range(25):
            if h >> i & 1:
                rr, cc = divmod(i, 5)
                g |= 1 << (rr * 5 + 4 - cc if m < 86 else (4 - rr) * 5 + cc)
    else:
        d = r.randrange(4)
        for cc in range(5):
            for j in range(r.randrange(0, 4)):
                g |= 1 << ((4 - j) * 5 + cc if d == 0 else j * 5 + cc if d == 1
                           else cc * 5 + j if d == 2 else cc * 5 + 4 - j)
    return g


def VISIBLE(j, g):
    """Is rule j satisfied VISIBLY rather than vacuously?  "the top row and the middle row
    are exactly the same" is technically true of two empty rows, and a kid reading such an
    example learns nothing, so the examples and the true candidate are always drawn from the
    pictures that show the relation."""
    t, q = U[j]
    if t not in (3, 4, 6):
        return True
    w = ROWS(g)
    A = (w, ["".join(x) for x in zip(*w)])[q > 1]
    if t == 3:
        return A[0] + A[1] + A[3] + A[4] != "." * 20
    if t == 4:
        return A[q % 2 * 2] != "....."
    return w[q] != "....."


# ---- tables built once per worker (not charged to max_generate_ms) ------------------------
_r0 = random.Random(20260905)
POOL = []
_seen = set()
while len(POOL) < 20000:
    _g = DRAW(_r0)
    _k = bin(_g).count("1")
    if 2 < _k < 15 and _g not in _seen:
        _seen.add(_g)
        POOL.append(_g)
MASK = []
XF = []
PID = {}
CNT = []
BM = []
_fe = []
_c = {}
for _g in POOL:
    MASK.append(MASKOF(_g))
    XF.append(XFEAT(_g))
    _f = FEAT(_g)
    _fe.append(_f)
    for _kv in _f.items():
        _c[_kv] = _c.get(_kv, 0) + 1
for _kv in _c:
    if _c[_kv] >= 300:                     # base rate >= 1.5 %; the players floor theirs at 5 %
        PID[_kv] = len(PID)
        CNT.append(_c[_kv])
for _f in _fe:
    _m = 0
    for _kv in _f.items():
        _j = PID.get(_kv)
        if _j is not None:
            _m |= 1 << _j
    BM.append(_m)
_fe = None
# the players' own surprise weight, -( (k+1) log p + 3 log(1-p) ), for k = 2 and 3 examples
SURP = []
for _n in CNT:
    _p = min(max((_n + .5) / 20001., 1e-4), .999)
    SURP.append((-(3 * math.log(_p) + 3 * math.log(1 - _p)),
                 -(4 * math.log(_p) + 3 * math.log(1 - _p))))
SAT = [[i for i, m in enumerate(MASK) if m >> j & 1 and VISIBLE(j, POOL[i])]
       for j in range(len(U))]
SATK = []
for _j in range(len(U)):
    _d = {}
    for _i in SAT[_j]:
        _d.setdefault(XF[_i][0], []).append(_i)
    SATK.append(_d)
BYK = {}
for _i, _x in enumerate(XF):
    BYK.setdefault(_x[0], []).append(_i)
BYT = {}
for _j, _r in enumerate(U):
    BYT.setdefault(_r[0], []).append(_j)
# the three CHEAP templates are drawn at double weight: they are the only rules a generic
# 5x5 predicate bank already holds, so they are the class's learnable slope (~35 % of clues,
# which puts the label-spending attacker at ~46 % instead of ~38 %).
TPLS = sorted(BYT) * 3 + list(CHEAP) * 2
K = 5                                       # candidates per lineup (revision 3, lever 1)


def RANKS(r, sat, dec, C, ne, EX):
    """Choose the true candidate and the K-1 decoys so that the TRUE one sits at a uniformly
    random place in FOUR orders the attacker can build (revision 3, lever 5):

    * the RARITY order (revision 2 sec.5c, and what both revision-2 players actually ran):
      keep every bank predicate true of all the examples (the set C) and of EXACTLY ONE
      candidate, and answer the candidate carrying the rarest one;
    * the COUNT order (revision 2 sec.2): how many example-consistent predicates each
      candidate satisfies;
    * the LOOK-ALIKE order: how many squares each candidate shares with the other four
      ("the odd one out" / "the medoid");
    * the FAMILY-RESEMBLANCE order: how many squares it shares with its nearest example.
    """
    CL = []
    b = C
    while b:
        l = b & -b
        CL.append(l.bit_length() - 1)
        b ^= l
    if not CL or len(dec) < K - 1:
        return None
    S = [SURP[p][ne] for p in CL]
    cs = {}

    def comp(i):
        v = cs.get(i)
        if v is None:
            m = BM[i]
            v = 0
            for k, p in enumerate(CL):
                if m >> p & 1:
                    v |= 1 << k
            cs[i] = v
        return v
    ag = {}

    def look(i, j):
        k = (i, j) if i < j else (j, i)
        v = ag.get(k)
        if v is None:
            v = ag[k] = 25 - bin(POOL[i] ^ POOL[j]).count("1")
        return v
    a1 = r.randrange(K); a2 = r.randrange(K); a3 = r.randrange(K); a4 = r.randrange(K)
    best = None
    bd = 99
    for _t in range(40):
        t = sat[r.randrange(len(sat))]
        pick = [t] + r.sample(dec, K - 1)
        mm = [comp(i) for i in pick]
        sc = []
        for a in range(K):
            u = mm[a]
            for b2 in range(K):
                if a != b2:
                    u &= ~mm[b2]
            x = -1.
            while u:
                l = u & -u
                k = l.bit_length() - 1
                if S[k] > x:
                    x = S[k]
                u ^= l
            sc.append(x)
        ov = [sum(look(pick[a], pick[b2]) for b2 in range(K) if b2 != a) for a in range(K)]
        nx = [max(look(pick[a], e) for e in EX) for a in range(K)]
        d = 3 * abs(sum(1 for a in range(1, K) if sc[a] > sc[0]) - a1) \
            + 2 * abs(sum(1 for a in range(1, K) if mm[a].bit_count() > mm[0].bit_count()) - a2) \
            + abs(sum(1 for a in range(1, K) if ov[a] > ov[0]) - a3) \
            + 2 * abs(sum(1 for a in range(1, K) if nx[a] > nx[0]) - a4)
        if d < bd:
            bd = d
            best = pick
            if d == 0:
                break
    out = [POOL[i] for i in best]
    r.shuffle(out)
    return out


def LINEUP(r, j, ex, C, tr):
    """K pictures with the SAME NUMBER OF MARKS, exactly one of which obeys the rule.  Every
    decoy breaks the rule and fires EXACTLY the same example-consistent excluded rules as the
    true candidate (revision 2 sec.5b, strong form); RANKS then aims the truth's place."""
    b = 1 << j
    d = SATK[j]
    ES = set(ex)
    ne = len(ex) - 2
    KS = [x for x in d if len(d[x]) > 2 and len(BYK.get(x, ())) > 200]
    r.shuffle(KS)
    for x in KS:
        st = d[x]
        SG = {}
        for i in (st if len(st) < 80 else r.sample(st, 80)):
            if i not in ES:
                SG.setdefault(TBITS(tr, XF[i]), []).append(i)
        if not SG:
            continue
        px = BYK[x]
        n = len(px)
        DG = {}
        hit = None
        sn = set()
        for _s in range(300):
            i = px[r.randrange(n)]
            if i in sn or MASK[i] & b or i in ES:
                continue
            sn.add(i)
            tb = TBITS(tr, XF[i])
            if SG.get(tb) is None:
                continue
            u = DG.setdefault(tb, [])
            u.append(i)
            if len(u) >= K + 4:
                hit = tb
                break
        if hit is None:
            if not DG:
                continue
            hit = max((len(v), k2) for k2, v in DG.items())[1]
            if len(DG[hit]) < K - 1:
                continue
        out = RANKS(r, SG[hit], DG[hit], C, ne, ex)
        if out:
            return out
    return None


def EXAMPLES(r, A, three):
    """A MINIMAL identifying set: together they leave exactly one rule of U alive, and no
    proper subset does.  A PAIR is tried first (revision 3, lever 2) and wins 94 % of the
    time; the pictures must differ in at least four squares."""
    if not three:
        for _t in range(40):
            T = r.sample(A, 2)
            if MASK[T[0]].bit_count() < 2 or MASK[T[1]].bit_count() < 2:
                continue
            if (MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[1]]).bit_count() != 1:
                continue
            if bin(POOL[T[0]] ^ POOL[T[1]]).count("1") < 4:
                continue
            return T
    for _t in range(40):
        T = r.sample(A, 3)
        m = MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[1]]
        if m.bit_count() < 2 or (MASK[T[0]] & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() < 2:
            continue
        if (MASK[T[1]] & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() < 2:
            continue
        if (m & MASK[T[2]]).bit_count() != 1:
            continue
        if min(bin(POOL[a] ^ POOL[b]).count("1") for a in T for b in T if a < b) < 4:
            continue
        return T
    return None


def PIC(g):
    return "\n".join(ROWS(g))


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(150):
        j = r.choice(BYT[r.choice(TPLS)])       # template first, then parameter
        A = SAT[j]
        if len(A) < 12:
            continue
        Ar = [i for i in A if MASK[i].bit_count() > 2]
        for _e in range(4):
            cand = Ar if (len(Ar) > 11 and r.random() < .5) else A
            best = EXAMPLES(r, cand, False)
            if best is None:
                break
            C = -1
            for i in best:
                C &= BM[i]
            line = LINEUP(r, j, best, C, TRAPS([XF[i] for i in best], U[j]))
            if line is not None:
                return "\n\n".join(PIC(POOL[i]) for i in best) + "\n\n" + \
                    "\n\n".join("%d\n%s" % (n + 1, PIC(g)) for n, g in enumerate(line))
    # never reached in 20 000 seeds, but kept scoreable all the same: the seed-0 clue, whose
    # single survivor is "every column of marks reaches the floor"
    return (".....\n.....\n.....\n#....\n#...#\n\n#.#.#\n....#\n.....\n....#\n#.#.#\n\n1\n..#..\n..#..\n"
            ".....\n..#..\n..#..\n\n2\n..##.\n.#...\n.....\n...#.\n.....\n\n3\n...#.\n.....\n##...\n....."
            "\n....#\n\n4\n.#...\n....#\n.....\n.....\n##...\n\n5\n.##..\n#....\n.....\n#....\n.....")
